title: Reverse a Vector with Swaps, Then Sum
statement: Read an integer n, then n integers into a vector. Reverse the vector in place with your own loop that uses swap. Do not use std::reverse. Print the reversed vector on one line, with single spaces between numbers. On the next line, print the sum of all numbers. If n is 0, print an empty line, then 0.
inputFormat: First line: integer n. Second line: n integers separated by spaces. If n is 0, the second line is missing or empty.
outputFormat: Line 1: the n integers in reversed order, separated by single spaces (empty line if n = 0). Line 2: the sum of the integers.
constraints: The sum can be larger than a 32-bit int
explanations: The numbers 1 2 3 4 5 become 5 4 3 2 1 after swapping the ends inward. The sum is 1+2+3+4+5 = 15.
Reversing 10 -3 7 0 gives 0 7 -3 10. The sum is 10-3+7+0 = 14. Negative numbers are added normally.
reference:
import sys

def main():
    t = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(t[0])
    a = [int(x) for x in t[1:1 + n]]
    i, j = 0, len(a) - 1
    while i < j:
        a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
        i += 1
        j -= 1
    print(" ".join(str(x) for x in a))
    print(sum(a))

main()
